questions.question: It was him who came running into the class room. The error of the sentence lies in -
questions.explanation: It was him এর পরিবর্তে It was he হবে। Copulative verb এর complement হওয়ার কারণে Nominative case বসাতে হবে।

questions.question: Read the sentence to find out whether there is any error in it. I intend to go straight back home, but I sort of wandered inside a bookstore.
questions.explanation: বাক্যে 'wandered' থেকে বুঝা যায় যে বাক্যটি Past tense এ। So, instead of 'intend', 'intended' is to be used here.

questions.question: Select the segment that contains a grammatical error. We love to just lay on the beach.
questions.explanation: Correct: We love to just lie on the beach. Lie/lay/lain is used without an object. Lay/laid/laid must have an object.

questions.question: Heliograph was an (a) instrument employed to (b) send signals (c) by reflecting (d) sunlight a mirror or mirrors. Find the error.
questions.explanation: by reflecting sunlight a mirror এর জায়গায় by reflecting sunlight with a mirror হবে।

questions.question: Students who wish to become a doctor must begin planning their studies long before they apply to medical school. Identify the incorrect segment.
questions.explanation: Subject plural + are/were/become + plural noun অনুসারে students (subject) plural হওয়ায় a doctor না হয়ে doctors হবে।

questions.question: Passive smoking is defined as the exposure of nonsmoker to environmental tobacco smoke. Find the error.
questions.explanation: Nonsmoker এককভাবে এখানে ভুল। এটা singular হিসেবে ব্যবহার করতে চাইলে এর পূর্বে 'a' দিতে হবে অথবা একে plural (nonsmokers) করতে হবে।

questions.question: If one plans to hike in the backcountry, you should prepare for the possibility of encountering a bear. Find the error.
questions.explanation: you should এর পরিবর্তে they should হবে। প্রথমে বলা হয়েছে If one plans, তাই they should ব্যবহার করতে হবে।

questions.question: Find the error part of the sentence. It is not difficult to believe that a man (A) who has lived in this city (B) for a long time (C) he will never feel at home anywhere else in the world (D)
questions.explanation: 'he will never feel at home anywhere else in the world' এই অংশ থেকে 'he' বাদ দিতে হবে। প্রদত্ত বাক্যের প্রধান কর্তা 'the man' এর বিপরীতে 'who' ব্যবহার করা হয়েছে।

questions.question: Find the error: I and my colleague / have carefully considered the important issues raised by / the report which you sent me and / we have decided to take the following action.

options.b: have carefully considered the important issues raised by
options.c: the report which you sent me and
options.d: we have decided to take the following

questions.explanation: Solution: Change, I and my colleague → My colleague and I.

questions.question: Find the error: The gambling stall / was a grand success / because almost everyone / tried their luck.
questions.explanation: Solution: Substitute, their → his/her. EVERYONE is a singular subject and must be followed by a singular pronoun.

questions.question: Find the error: There are / no conducted tours / for tourist to visit all the / important places.

options.c: for tourist to visit all the

questions.correct_answer_text: for tourist to visit all the
questions.explanation: Solution: Replace, tourist by tourists.

questions.question: Find the error: This girl / wrote an essay / so well that / her teacher was exceedingly pleased with her.

options.d: her teacher was exceedingly pleased with her

questions.explanation: Solution: Substitute, 'an' by 'the'. The sentence lays emphasis on essay.

questions.question: Find the error: Everyone of the students / has bought / his / identity card.
questions.explanation: Solution: Change, everyone → each one. When the number is limited, 'each one' will be better usage than 'everyone'.

questions.question: Find the error: As he stood / below the shower / the sharp jets of / ice cold water revived his spirit.

options.d: ice cold water revived his spirit

questions.correct_answer_text: ice cold water revived his spirit
questions.explanation: Solution: Change, spirit → spirits. Spirits refers to a person's mood or attitude.

questions.question: Find the error: I have / two sister-in-laws / whose husbands / are all well settled.
questions.explanation: Solution: Change, sister-in-laws → sisters-in-law. Plural of compound words is formed by adding 's' in the first constituent.

questions.question: Find the error: I told him / the story / in details / to make him understand it fully.

options.d: to make him understand it fully

questions.explanation: Solution: Change, details → detail.

questions.question: Find the error: Vijay is / very much / sorry about her misconduct.
questions.explanation: Solution: Very is used without 'much' before adjectives in the positive degree. Correct: Vijay is very sorry about her misconduct.

questions.question: Find the error: Our knowledge of history does not come to / Our help and some times we / even fail to remember / who invented America.

options.a: Our knowledge of history does not come to
options.b: Our help and some times we

questions.explanation: Solution: who discovered America.

questions.question: Find the error: The Moon may be the best place / to look for aliens as their / footprints on their surface would / last far longer than radio signals.

options.a: The Moon may be the best place
options.b: to look for aliens as their
options.d: last far longer than radio signals

questions.explanation: Solution: change, footprints on their surface would → footprints on its surface would.

questions.question: Find out the error: The ruling party stood (A)/ for implementation of the Bill (B)/ and was ready to stake their political existence (C)/ No error(D).
questions.explanation: 'and was ready to stake their political existence' এই অংশে ভুল। Their এর পরিবর্তে It's হবে।

questions.question: Find the error: Summons were / issued yesterday / by Sessions judge / against the suspected thief.
questions.explanation: Solution: Change, Summons were → Summons was. The word Summons is singular and should carry a singular verb.

questions.question: Find the error: The fact of me/ being a stranger/ does not excuse his conduct.
questions.explanation: Solution: Objective Case should be replaced by Possessive Case. Correct: the fact of my being.

questions.question: Find the error: An Indian ship / laden with merchandise / got drowned in the Pacific Ocean.

options.c: got drowned in the Pacific Ocean

questions.correct_answer_text: got drowned in the Pacific Ocean
questions.explanation: Solution: sank in the Pacific Ocean.

questions.question: Find the error: One of the members / expressed doubt if / the Minister was an atheist.
questions.explanation: Solution: expressed doubt that.

questions.question: Find the error: Do the roses in your garden smell / more sweetly / than those in ours?

options.a: Do the roses in your garden smell

questions.explanation: Solution: sweeter.

questions.question: Find the error: The students were / awaiting for / the arrival of the chief guest.

options.c: the arrival of the chief guest

questions.explanation: Solution: awaiting (no preposition needed).

questions.question: Find the error: They have been / very close friends / until they quarrelled.
questions.explanation: Solution: 'They had been'.

questions.question: Find the error: You must / remember me / to post this letter.
questions.explanation: Solution: remind me.

questions.question: Find the error: I shall certainly / write you / when I shall reach New Delhi.

options.c: when I shall reach New Delhi

questions.correct_answer_text: when I shall reach New Delhi
questions.explanation: Solution: when I reach New Delhi.

questions.question: Find out whether there is any grammatical error: The crews were on board, / and they soon busied themselves / in preparing to meet the storm.

options.c: in preparing to meet the storm

questions.correct_answer_text: in preparing to meet the storm
questions.explanation: Solution: in preparing to face the storm.

questions.question: Find out whether there is any grammatical error: Troy was taken by Greeks / this formed the basis of a story / which has become famous.

options.b: this formed the basis of a story

questions.explanation: Solution: Troy was taken by the Greeks.

questions.question: Find out whether there is any grammatical error: Twice twelve / makes / twenty-four.
questions.explanation: Solution: make.

questions.question: Find out whether there is any grammatical error: If I were him, / I would have taught / those cheats a lesson.
questions.explanation: Solution: If I were he, I would have taught those cheats a lesson.

questions.question: Find out whether there is any grammatical error: We are four brothers and sisters living in this house / but neither of us is / satisfied with it.

options.a: We are four brothers and sisters living in this house

questions.explanation: Solution: but none of us are.

questions.question: Find out whether there is any grammatical error: The scientist must follow / his hunches and his data / wherever it may lead.
questions.explanation: Solution: 'whenever they may lead'.

questions.question: Find out whether there is any grammatical error: Will you be / at Board meeting / on next Wednesday?
questions.explanation: Solution: next Wednesday (remove 'on').

questions.question: Find out whether there is any grammatical error: At last the rain ceased / and the sky was / cleared by clouds / and lightning.
questions.explanation: Solution: cleared of clouds.

questions.question: Find out whether there is any grammatical error: When I stood up spontaneously / and questioned the speaker; / someone commented that / it was a boldly step.
questions.explanation: Solution: it was a bold step.

questions.question: Patrician is -

options.b: the male head of a family
options.c: a person who loves his country very much

questions.explanation: 'Patrician' refers to a person of noble birth or high social rank. Option b = patriarch, c = patriot, d = patron.

questions.question: A person who believes that all events are predetermined and human free will is an illusion -
questions.explanation: A Determinist believes all events are determined by prior causes and free will is an illusion. A Fatalist believes fate controls outcomes.

questions.question: A person who secretly collects and enjoys observing private lives of others -
questions.explanation: A Voyeur derives pleasure from watching others in private moments. An Exhibitionist shows themselves publicly, a Narcissist is self-obsessed, a Recluse avoids society.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: "To blow hot and cold"

options.c: To be inconsistent in opinion or attitude

questions.correct_answer_text: To be inconsistent in opinion or attitude
questions.explanation: 'To blow hot and cold' means to keep changing one's opinion — sometimes supporting something and sometimes opposing it.

questions.question: Choose the synonym of "Nexus".
questions.explanation: Nexus means a connection or series of connections linking things. Synonyms include junction, link, and linkage.

questions.question: Antonym of "Philogynist"?
questions.explanation: A Philogynist loves or admires women. The antonym is Misogynist — a person with prejudice against women.

questions.question: The correct analogy of "Enfranchise : Emancipate" is -
questions.explanation: Enfranchise and Emancipate are synonyms (both mean to free). Similarly, Bondage (slavery) and Thraldom (enslavement) are synonymous.

questions.question: The best analogy of "Tacit : Words" is -
questions.explanation: Tacit = understood without words (absence of Words). Unanimous = total agreement (absence of Disagreements). Both pairs show a word that negates the second concept.

questions.question: SOOT : COMBUSTION ::
questions.explanation: Soot is the byproduct of Combustion. Similarly, Sawdust is the byproduct of Woodcutting. Analogy: byproduct : process.

questions.question: Which of the following words is connected to an argument?
questions.explanation: Altercation means a noisy argument. Alias = alternative name, Alienation = isolation, Alteration = change.

questions.question: Fill in the gap: Before leaving for the workplace, I spent ____ with my children.
questions.explanation: 'Some time' (two words) means a period of time. 'Sometime' = at an unspecified time, 'sometimes' = occasionally.

questions.question: Pick out the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Inundate', meaning to overwhelm or flood. The other options have incorrect letters.

questions.question: Priya bears _____ the first position.
questions.explanation: 'Bear away' means to win or carry off a prize. 'Bear on' = relate to, 'bear out' = confirm, 'bear with' = tolerate.

questions.question: The antonym of 'dear' is -
questions.explanation: 'Dear' means beloved or expensive. Its antonym is 'cheap' (inexpensive).

questions.question: The antonym of 'confide' is -
questions.explanation: 'Confide' means to trust someone with a secret. Its antonym is 'suspect' (to distrust or doubt).

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'Few and far between'?
questions.explanation: The idiom 'few and far between' means occurring rarely or infrequently.

questions.question: "Harp on" means -

options.d: talk about the same subject repeatedly

questions.correct_answer_text: talk about the same subject repeatedly
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'harp on' means to talk persistently and tediously about the same subject.

questions.question: One who specializes in the ways diseases spread among people -
questions.explanation: An Epidemiologist studies how diseases spread among populations. An Entomologist studies insects, an Archaeologist studies human history.

questions.question: 'Milk-and-water' means -

options.a: Something that is very easy to perform.
options.d: Lacking the will or ability to act effectively.

questions.correct_answer_text: Lacking the will or ability to act effectively.
questions.explanation: The idiom 'milk-and-water' describes something feeble, insipid, or lacking strength and conviction.

questions.question: A quotation placed at the beginning of a work to suggest its theme -
questions.explanation: An 'Epigraph' is a quotation at the beginning of a literary work to suggest its theme. An 'Epigram' is a short witty saying, an 'Epistle' is a formal letter.

questions.question: Conspicuous means ___
questions.explanation: 'Conspicuous' means clearly visible or attracting notice. 'Hidden' is its antonym.

questions.question: To accustom oneself to a foreign climate -
questions.explanation: 'Acclimatize' means to become accustomed to a new climate. 'Adapt' is more general, 'Adopt' = to take up, 'Accustom' = to make familiar through habit.
